name: The Suburbs
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Nine songs on red vinyl in 1978 were the first record Twin/Tone ever pressed. Sixteen years on, a live album by the same band was the last.

eras.title: Home from Los Angeles, red vinyl next
eras.text: Two Minneapolis suburbanites come back from Los Angeles, pick up three players from a band called the Tsetse Flies, and end up on the first record Twin/Tone ever puts out.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band) · PopMatters: The Suburbs Celebrate Personal History
years.h: [[Chan Poling|ee72fe22-4355-48be-9a94-fd5093050d63]] and [[Beej Chaney|0376e2dc-f99e-4fdc-8a92-7de62c781095]] come home from Los Angeles and start a band
years.p: Back in Minneapolis they join drummer Hugo Klaers, guitarist Bruce C. Allen and bassist Michael Halliday, who had been playing together as the Tsetse Flies.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the Suburbs to November 1977. Poling and Chaney had been in a Los Angeles band called the Technocats with Su Tissue of the Suburban Lawns, and Klaers, Allen and Halliday had been playing together as the Tsetse Flies.

Poling has said he studied contemporary classical music at CalArts but found punk and new wave more compelling. He credits Chris Osgood of the [[The Suicide Commandos|eb7988a4-4a66-4320-a6ea-d17da0da88ac]] with pointing the band toward Twin/Tone.

years.src: The Current: We started a scene · Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band)
years.h: Jay's Longhorn Bar takes on a band that only plays originals
years.p: Owner Jay Berine hesitated until he saw the crowds at their basement shows, then made the Suburbs regulars.
years.xp:
Klaers told The Current the basement parties drew 400 to 500 people, which persuaded Berine.

Klaers: "The Longhorn held 400 people, and the same 200 were there every night." Wikipedia adds that Bruce Springsteen, in town on the tour for The River, came to see the band and nearly joined them for an encore.

years.src: Diffuser: April 17, 1978: The Day the Suburbs Hit the Shelves · Wikipedia: The Suburbs EP · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: Nine songs in about 16 minutes become Twin/Tone's first record
years.p: Pressed on red vinyl as TTR 7801 and released April 17, 1978, one of three EPs the new label put out at once.
years.xp:
The EP was cut at Blackberry Way in Minneapolis, produced by Twin/Tone co-founder Paul Stark. The label put out three EPs at once (Fingerprints, Spooks and the Suburbs), and the first pressing was 2,500 copies on red vinyl.

Peter Jesperson recalled the Longhorn's owner saying the band sounded like they had stepped right off the playground and onto the stage, which Jesperson thought would make a good slogan. Twin/Tone's own discography lists the release date as April 17, 1978.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bruce C. Allen · Wikipedia: Twin/Tone Records
years.h: Guitarist Bruce C. Allen designs the label's logo too
years.p: Allen draws the Twin/Tone logo and the Suburbs' own, and does art direction on the compilation Big Hits of Mid-America, Volume Three.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Allen with the Suburbs logo, the Twin/Tone logo and art direction on the compilation Big Hits of Mid-America, Volume Three. Tiny Mix Tapes and Wikipedia also credit him with the cover of the [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]] album Let It Be.

eras.title: The house band of Twin/Tone
eras.text: Three records and a run of dance singles on the label they helped launch. The sound goes from jittery new wave to double-album sprawl to club mixes.

years.h: "World War III" is the 7-inch that follows the EP
years.p: Released June 26, 1979 as TTR 7909, with "Change Agent" on the B-side. Paul Stark again produces at Blackberry Way.

years.src: Wikipedia: In Combo · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: In Combo gives the band a first full album
years.p: Paul Stark produces 31 minutes at Blackberry Way for Twin/Tone, catalog TTR 8014.
years.xp:
It came out January 20, 1980. AllMusic's Stewart Mason called it one of the pioneering releases of the American post-punk indie scene and, in his words, probably the band's greatest vinyl moment. Trouser Press's Ira Robbins heard signs of incipient musical greatness.

Wikipedia notes the record showed the Minneapolis scene of the early 1980s had room for more than the guitar-driven aggression of the Replacements and Hüsker Dü.

years.cap: The Suburbs on stage at the Peppermint Lounge, 1981
years.src: Wikipedia: Credit in Heaven · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: Credit in Heaven stretches to 17 songs and two records
years.p: Jazz, funk and disco work their way in, and some tracks run near ten minutes. Recorded April to June 7, 1981 with Paul Stark.
years.xp:
Saxophonist Max Ray guests, and "Music for Boys" (6:47) became a local radio hit; a dance mix followed as a 12-inch on June 24, 1982. AllMusic's Mark Deming said the album's reach sometimes exceeds its grasp, and called it an under-appreciated milestone of Midwestern new wave. Trouser Press's Ira Robbins: "A highly recommended stunner."

It won Best LP at the 1982 Minnesota Music Awards. Twin/Tone lists the release as TTR 8125/6.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dream Hog EP · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: "Waiting" goes out as a 12-inch and the dance floors pick it up
years.p: Producer Steven Greenberg, the man behind Lipps Inc.'s "Funkytown," remixes it with Paul Stark. The Dream Hog EP follows on November 30.
years.xp:
Twin/Tone released the 12-inch as TTR 8229. Dream Hog is four songs, including "Roll Over City" and "The Best Is Over," plus a club mix, released as TTR 8230 and recorded at the Stark/Mudge Mobile Unit warehouse in Brooklyn Center.

Greenberg then took the band to Phonogram, and the EP was reissued on Mercury.

eras.title: Mercury, A&M, and out
eras.text: Producer Steven Greenberg walks them to Phonogram. Four years and two major-label albums later, the band is done.

years.big: "We've always wanted to sell records, to join the big time."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band) · Wikipedia: Love Is the Law (Suburbs album)
years.h: Mercury reissues Dream Hog and the Twin/Tone years end
years.p: Chan Poling tells the press the band loved what Twin/Tone had done for them. Greenberg had made the introduction to Phonogram.
years.xp: Mercury put Dream Hog out as the band's first major-label release. They recorded Love Is the Law that June and July.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Is the Law (Suburbs album) · The Suburbs: Bio
years.h: A dead toreador on the cover, a dance-rock record inside
years.p: Love Is the Law, recorded June and July 1983 with Greenberg and Paul Stark and out in March 1984, wins two Minnesota Music Awards: one for the album, one for the title single.
years.xp:
The cover is Manet's painting The Dead Toreador. Poling told Cashbox the band liked the contrast of a warm title over a cold image. The album adds horns and a harder rock edge, with songs like "Perfect Communist" and "Monster Man." Trouser Press's Ira Robbins called it easily the band's apex.

The title song later became an anthem for the marriage equality movement, and the band's bio says as much. Wikipedia notes it was used on Roseanne, in Darlene's prom scene, in 1993.

years.h: "Rattle My Bones" goes to work for Target and the Vikings
years.p: The Love Is the Law track later turns up in Target ads and becomes a Minnesota Vikings home-game staple.

years.h: Bobby Z. of Prince's Revolution produces the A&M album
years.p: Credited as "Robert Brent," he cuts Suburbs at Metro Studios in Minneapolis, the band's only record for A&M.
years.xp: Reviews split. Stewart Mason of AllMusic said the production smothered what made the band good; Ira Robbins found it another powerful record, with less urgency than before. It was never issued on CD.

years.h: After ten years, the band calls it quits
years.p: MPR reports the Suburbs disbanded in 1987; Wikipedia says the A&M record never got the radio play the label wanted.

eras.title: Chaney goes west, the band reunites anyway
eras.text: A best-of, a reunion and one last record for the label that started with them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Beej Chaney · The Current: Beej Chaney of The Suburbs has died
years.h: Beej Chaney settles in Los Angeles
years.p: The distance shapes the reunited band, per Wikipedia. Chaney later buys a studio in Malibu.
years.xp: Chaney released the EP Reckless Heart in 1992 and the album Windows in 2003. He bought Shangri-La, the Malibu studio, in the late 1990s and owned it until he sold it to Rick Rubin in 2011. The Current lists Weezer, Metallica, Kings of Leon and Mark Knopfler among those who recorded there.

years.h: A best-of called Ladies and Gentlemen, The Suburbs Have Left the Building
years.p: Twin/Tone issues the CD on November 3, 1992 as TTR 89232, pulling together the band's early records.

years.src: MPR News: Allen, guitarist for Suburbs, dies at 54 · The Current: The Suburbs announce first new album in 27 years · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: The Suburbs start playing shows again
years.p: MPR News dates the reunion to 1993. After that it is one or two shows a year.
years.xp: Chan Poling told The Current the band did one or two shows a year for two decades after the breakup. One of them, on April 24, 1993 at First Avenue, was recorded and became most of a live album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Twin/Tone Records · Twin/Tone: The Suburbs
years.h: Twin/Tone's last release is a live Suburbs album
years.p: Viva! Suburbs! Live at First Avenue comes out November 21, 1994 as TTR 89288. Wikipedia calls it the label's final official release.
years.xp: Most of it was recorded at First Avenue on April 24, 1993. Twin/Tone put out over 300 records by roughly 100 bands over 17 years, per Wikipedia. The label was revived in 2017 for a Suicide Commandos album.

eras.title: Beejtar Records, and a loss
eras.text: The band puts its first albums back out on its own label, then loses the guitarist who drew its logo.

years.h: Beejtar Records puts three early albums back on CD
years.p: In Combo, Credit in Heaven and Love Is the Law return on Chaney's label, followed by the 2003 best-of Chemistry Set: Songs of the Suburbs 1977–1987.

years.src: MPR News: Allen, guitarist for Suburbs, dies at 54 · Slicing Up Eyeballs: Bruce Allen of The Suburbs, 1955-2009 · The Current: The Suburbs announce first new album in 27 years
years.h: Bruce C. Allen dies at 54
years.p: The guitarist dies December 7, 2009, after a week in the hospital with internal bleeding; MPR reports he was taken off life support.
years.xp:
Slicing Up Eyeballs reported that he had had organ failure, complications from triple bypass surgery the year before. Bassist Michael Halliday, who had arthritis, also stepped away that year.

Peter Jesperson: "They never made that big splash elsewhere, but locally they were like the Rolling Stones." Steve Brantseg and Steve Price joined for a benefit concert in Allen's honor.

eras.title: On their own money
eras.text: Kickstarter pays for the comeback, and the band keeps playing after losing a co-founder.

years.src: MPR News: Chan Poling and The Suburbs use Kickstarter · Star Tribune: The 'Burbs are back · The Current: The Suburbs announce first new album in 27 years
years.h: Backers pay $73,000 for the first new Suburbs album in 27 years
years.p: The Kickstarter for Si Sauvage clears its $65,000 goal.
years.xp:
Poling said going independent avoided the recoup trap of the 1980s, when a single video could cost $350,000. Rewards ran from a $10 download to a $10,000 private concert; two backers bought that one.

The band was Poling, Chaney, Klaers, Brantseg and Price with guests Janey Winterbauer and Aby Wolf. The Current has the release as August 27 and Wikipedia has November 19, so this page says only 2013.

years.src: PopMatters: The Suburbs Celebrate Personal History · Wikipedia: The Suburbs (band)
years.h: Hey Muse! arrives without Chaney
years.p: Chaney took a leave of absence in August 2014, per Wikipedia, and the band crowdfunded the record.
years.xp:
Poling told PopMatters the closing song, "When We Were Young," is the most literal thing he has written. He also said he is not going to get in a van and suffer for his art anymore.

Chaney's absence is stated inconsistently: Isthmus and PopMatters say he left; Wikipedia says leave of absence.

years.h: The Suburbs are the first band back in First Avenue
years.p: Two sold-out shows in the 7th Street Entry follow the pandemic closure, tied to the album Poets Party.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Poets Party as their seventh studio album. The band has a star on First Avenue's exterior wall.

years.big: "There's not a guitarist in the world that plays a guitar like Beej."
years.src: Star Tribune: Beej Chaney, Suburbs co-founder, dies · The Current: Beej Chaney of The Suburbs has died
years.h: Beej Chaney dies swimming off Hermosa Beach at 67
years.p: Drummer Hugo Klaers on Chaney, to the Star Tribune. Officials ruled the death an accident; Chaney swam in the ocean daily.
years.xp:
He was finishing a rockabilly album with Robby Vee.

The band's statement called him a true original who lived his art.

years.src: The Current: Interview: The Suburbs on A Pagan Ritual
yt: "Love Is the Law", live on Minnesota PBS STAGE
years.h: Two Cabooze nights from 1983 finally come out as a live album
years.p: A Pagan Ritual: Live at The Cabooze 1983 was recorded by Paul Stark's mobile truck. The band plays three nights at the Parkway Theater in May 2026.
years.xp:
Steve Price found the tapes on a hard drive Stark had kept, with material from the band's whole catalog, and Peter Jesperson helped pick the 10 tracks.

Poling: "The Cabooze was not a place that our kind of bands would play." Hugo Klaers said the band was especially tight, and that Bruce Allen was "a special and gifted guitar player."
